skills.name: Transport development in Cameroon: connecting the full journey

note.text: Developing a transport system requires more than adding a major corridor. Local access, terminal capacity, maintenance, transfers and reliable services determine whether a complete journey works. Different users may gain or lose differently. A port improvement does not automatically repair inland roads; a railway corridor does not automatically provide collection from every farm.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to evaluate a multimodal proposal using access, transfers and maintenance. Builds on: Cameroon routes and access inequalities. Leads to: map-network practicals.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Developing a transport system requires more than adding a major corridor. Local access, terminal capacity, maintenance, transfers and reliable services determine whether a complete journey works. Different users may gain or lose differently. A port improvement does not automatically repair inland roads; a railway corridor does not automatically provide collection from every farm.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented Cameroon proposal, produce travels by a local road to a depot and continues towards a port. The trunk connection improves, but the access road still floods seasonally. The whole-chain assessment includes spoilage, transfer handling and environmental effects as well as the improved link. No actual project performance or present road condition is claimed.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Trace origin, access link, transfer node, trunk link and destination. Identify the weakest stated connection. Compare a proposed intervention against that constraint, then record remaining uncertainties and affected users.

pick.q: An invented trunk route improves, but the farm access road is blocked. What limits delivery?
w: The trunk improvement proves delivery is guaranteed
A port name removes the blockage
Only straight-line distance matters
e: The chain still contains a blocked link.
A name does not create access.
Usable connections matter, not distance alone.

pick.q: A fictional proposal changes from road to rail at a depot. What should its cost comparison include?
w: Assume all transfers are free and instant
Only the colour of each vehicle
Ignore how goods reach the depot
e: Transfers may add cost or time.
Vehicle colour does not establish transport performance.
Origin access is part of the journey.

pick.q: A fictional route benefits exporters but increases noise beside homes. What assessment fits?
pick.r: Compare benefits and costs for the affected groups
w: Exporter gains prove nobody bears a cost
Noise means no benefit can exist
Ignore households outside the firm
e: Benefits to one group do not remove costs to another.
Benefits and costs can coexist.
External effects concern people outside the firm.
pick.y: Evaluate distribution as well as total activity.
